t0: Browse a {project}'s code here: its files, the history of each, who changed which line, and the branches with the rules that protect them.
t1: Every {project} you add will show its files and commits here once Launchway reads the repository itself. Today it reads only the pipeline file.
t2: Read a proposed change, comment, see which checks passed, and merge it when the rules are met. A blocked merge will say which rule and what unblocks it.
t3: A change under review appears here when a pull request starts a run of a {project}. Runs of pull requests exist today, and are listed under Activity.
t4: List the packaged deployment descriptions your pipelines build, with their settings and the applications that use each version.
t5: A chart appears here when a pipeline step packages one and pushes it to a {registry} that Launchway can read.
t6: List the plain files your pipelines produce, such as installers and archives, with their size, who made them and where they were used.
t7: Files appear here when a step declares them as {artifacts}. {Artifacts} of a run can be read on the {run}'s own page today.
t8: Show your machines, which operating system image each runs, whether a new image is staged and waiting for a restart, and what each has run.
t9: A host appears here when it reports in to Launchway. Hosts that do the work of {runs} are listed today under Settings, {Runners}.
t10: List the operating system images your machines start from, each built and scanned by a pipeline like a container image, and which hosts run it.
t11: An image appears here when a pipeline builds one. Container images are listed today under Images.
t12: Draw what really talks to what: the services, the requests between them, how many fail and how slow they are, so a person can see where a problem starts.
t13: The map fills in from the numbers your signal sources hold. Add a source that holds request metrics, and the services you {deploy:do} will appear on it.
t15: Answer one question: is traffic protected, and is anyone attacking? Signs of attack come first with their evidence, then the limits on each route.
t16: Routes and their limits appear here once Launchway can read the gateway in front of your services, through a signal source.
t17: Show whether each service meets its target, and how much failure the target still allows this month, so a team knows when to slow down.
t18: A service appears here with a target you set, once a signal source gives its error and speed numbers. Verify steps already read such sources today.
t19: List the switches that turn a feature on for some visitors, show where each is on and for whom, and let a person turn one off in seconds without a new release.
t20: A toggle appears here when your applications report it. Nothing reports toggles to Launchway yet.
t21: Lay out what is changing and when: planned releases, {hold} windows and what already happened, so a team does not release into a bad hour.
t22: Changes appear on the calendar when a release is planned. Today the {runs} that {deploy:do} are listed under Activity and each deployment under Deployments.
t23: Keep one record per change: what, why, who gave {clearance}, what the evidence said and how it went. Auditors read it; nobody has to write it by hand.
t24: A record is made for every release that goes through a {clearance} rule. Decisions already taken are in the {logbook} today.
t25: Say when nothing may be released, such as month end or a holiday, and show the window on the calendar and on every {deploy:do} that it blocks.
t26: A window you add here blocks {deploy:does} to the places you choose. No {hold} windows are defined yet.
t27: Say which changes need whose {clearance}, by risk and by place, in plain sentences, and show a person exactly which rule applies to their change.
t28: A rule appears here when you write one. Steps that wait for {clearance} in a pipeline, and the rules that judge a {run}, work today.
t29: Connect the system where your {organization} records change requests, so a release links to its request and a request closes itself when the release is healthy.
t30: Connected tickets appear on each change record. Nothing is connected yet, and the connection is not built yet.
